statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 11% after the Oct 7 intraday decline fully retraced into the close and the first Globex hour held a 51-point range, while Stress stays elevated at 47% on long Treasury yields near 24-year highs, weak breadth and Brent close to $100.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published around the Oct 8 jobless claims print and the US cash open, where conditional risk is highest, and the 17:00Z 30-year bond auction is flagged as a secondary long-end checkpoint. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 dip fully retraces into the close as Globex opens quiet and long yields ease off 24-year highs
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 31,160.08, down 0.21% or 64.61 points, after opening at 30,976.25, falling to 30,904.46 and recovering to finish only 10 points below the 31,170.12 session high. The full retracement of an intraday decline of about 1% is the single most important structural observation for this assessment. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.36% intraday, its highest since April 2002, and the 30-year reached 5.73%, the highest since May 2002, before both eased into the close with the 30-year settling near 5.66%. The September FOMC minutes showed most participants judging that another rate increase would likely be appropriate by year end, with roughly 17% odds priced for the October meeting; yields drifted off their highs rather than extending after the release. VIX closed at 15.08 inside a 14.97-16.01 range, so the intraday volatility spike decayed. Breadth was materially weaker than the headline index decline implied, with the Russell 2000 down 1.31% against a 0.21% Nasdaq-100 fall, and bitcoin fell 2.64%. Megacaps held up: Nvidia closed 0.74% lower and both Nvidia and AMD finished less than 1% below record highs. Brent settled at 100.81, down 0.38%, and WTI at 88.81, down 1.30%, with Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks cited as a standing geopolitical backdrop rather than a fresh escalation. In the first hour of the new Globex session, NQ December futures traded at 31,449.50, up 0.15%, inside a 31,403.00-31,454.00 range. Taken together, the evidence shows an elevated-Stress environment driven by the long end of the curve and by weak breadth, but no persistent one-way price path: the decline retraced, volatility decayed and the overnight reopen is orderly. Tail is therefore held at the low-band floor while Stress stays elevated. The shared Finviz supporting-context file was stale and only partially collected, so it was not used; the assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours carry a complete published Claude record with no unavailable slots. Scores sat at a Tail floor of 10 to 14 through the Globex evening, the Asian session and the European morning. Tail then rose into the WATCH band at 21 to 23 with a trend-down mode between 11:00Z and 14:00Z as the Nasdaq-100 fell toward its 30,904.46 session low. From 15:00Z the mode returned to mixed and Tail declined steadily to 12 by 22:00Z as the decline retraced into the cash close. Stress ran between 45 and 54 throughout, peaking with the intraday decline and easing only partially, which is consistent with a difficult but mean-reverting environment rather than a pathological one.
outlookSummary: The published 24-hour path stays inside the EA_ON band throughout. Scores hold near a Tail floor of 10 across the Asian session, then step up gradually through the European morning as the scheduled Waller remarks and US pre-market positioning approach. Conditional risk peaks at a Tail of 17 in the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours, where the 12:30Z jobless claims print is immediately followed by the 13:30Z US cash open; those two hours plus the 12:00Z release hour carry an event/whipsaw mode. A secondary step-up is published for the 17:00Z hour, which contains a 30-year bond auction and the Musalem speech, because the long end of the curve has been the dominant driver of this week's equity pressure. Risk then declines through the US afternoon and back toward the overnight floor after the cash close. Every figure beyond the current clock-hour is conditional and assumes an orderly, two-way price path; a failed retracement, repeated extension or price holding a session extreme would invalidate the published decline.
